fields.why: Prevalence is reported and tested across 3+ levels of age, education, income, employment, race/ethnicity and sexual identity.
All four are SPDs with 3+ groups (sex is a pair; ADL/IADL disability is clinical here).

Trend tests (orthogonal contrasts) apply only to the ordinal variables, so the flag on race and sexual identity is a false alarm; side by side fits since no claim across those groups rests on a test, though pairwise (all pairs) is also defensible because pairwise t-tests are stated for all subgroups and the Table 2 note equates them with non-overlapping CIs.

brief_issues: When a blanket 'pairwise t-tests' method plus a note equating results with non-overlapping CIs covers nominal groups on which no claim is made, the brief does not say whether that is side by side or pairwise (all pairs).
